text: The council approved the motion to award contracts for the purchase and delivery of new tires with an annual aggregate amount not to exceed $770,000 citywide.
The council will discuss a procurement study and allocate $250,000 for it later in the day.
The council will consider increasing local business preference in future RFPs, with a proposed increase from 5% to 15%.
There is a risk that local businesses may not receive a significant portion of the contract, despite the intent to support them.
The current local business preference may not be sufficient to meaningfully impact the local economy.

The City Council approved the ordinance establishing a 12-month moratorium on the issuance of building permits for new residential standalone construction along commercial and transportation corridors in West Long Beach.
The ordinance was declared urgent and will take effect immediately.
The matter will be referred to the Planning Commission and planning staff to initiate a study of potential amendments to existing zoning and building regulations.
Planning Commission and planning staff will conduct a study to align zoning and building regulations with the city's more recent land use and urban design elements of the general plan.
The moratorium could impact development timelines and potentially affect housing supply in the targeted areas.
There is a risk that the study may take longer than expected, delaying any potential updates to zoning and building regulations.

The council supports the execution of a Second Amendment to the Exclusive Negotiation Agreement with Howard CDB for the continuation of negotiations on the proposed development of the former Long Beach Armory.
Continue working with developers to finalize the project agreement and secure necessary grants.
Support the adaptive reuse of the Armory Building and the inclusion of 100% affordable housing.
The project may face delays due to the need for additional time to secure state and infrastructure grants.
There could be challenges in maintaining the momentum of negotiations with developers.
The council voted to postpone item 52 to March 2nd.
The postponed item 52 will be reviewed by the community for 90 days with an opportunity for public comment.
Postponing the item may delay the implementation of the shelter animal health improvement plan.
The council adopted a resolution to address certain natural gas transmission rates.
The council adopted a resolution to increase the Low-Income Gas discount rate from 5% to 20% citywide.
The council approved a memorandum of understanding with the Service Employees International Union (Local 71721) citywide.
Follow up on the December 1st meeting agenda to determine what items will be discussed.
Raising utility rates during a pandemic may pose financial risks to low-income residents.

The council approved the recommendation to increase appropriations in the Special Advertising and Promotion Fund group in the City Manager Department by $6,000 to support the annual Giving Gala 2020 event at the Long Beach Exchange.
The City Manager Department is to use the additional $6,000 for the support of the annual Giving Gala 2020 event at the Long Beach Exchange.
No specific risks were identified in the discussion, though the approval of additional funds involves the usual financial risk associated with event planning.
The council concluded the public hearing and adopted a resolution amending the master fee and charges schedule for standby fire safety officer fees related to special events and filming citywide.
The fire safety officer fees will be revised to provide full cost recovery for staffing costs, with consumables and equipment maintenance costs removed and included in the citywide fee schedule.
There is a potential for increased costs if the revised fee structure does not adequately cover staffing expenses.

The motion to increase appropriations in the general fund group and the Economic Development Department by $25,000 to support the creation of a community vision for business corridor improvements on historic Pine Avenue and the North Pine Neighborhood was approved.
Councilwoman Gonzales will present the recommendation following her arrival from a graduation event.
The council voted to oppose Proposition Six, which seeks to repeal the 2017 tax initiative and voter approval for future gas and vehicle taxes.
The City Attorney is tasked with preparing a resolution to formally oppose Proposition Six.

Opposing Proposition Six could result in the loss of significant state funding for infrastructure projects, including $8 million annually for streets and roads, which could grow to $11 million by FY 20 and beyond.
